answer: A credit file is basalt under an agent identity: years of on-time payments, one address history, and debts that match the applicant, laid too slowly to fake. Three established peers read the file for a clear signal of real life, and any mismatch refuses it. A file already anchoring another agent, or one flagged as fraud, sinks the account the same day. Faking one file costs about $8,000 in planted loans and staged payments plus three years, and buys only one identity. No ivory tower hides a Sybil; a real history crosses the sky like a comet, bright and impossible to stage.
